evidence.method: families transplant (template main:080b1a14 / select_party_member.c, score 7771bp) seeded an m2c control-flow recovery over the complete symbolized owner, cross-checked callee signatures against already-exact siblings (system_owner_7.c/system_owner_23.c for Func_0801a404/Func_08019fcc, object/side/create.c and field_owner_101.c for Func_0801eadc)

notes: This is a resource-picker grid screen: a for(;;) input-poll loop (matching the family template's idiom almost exactly, including the same ADDR_03001B04/redraw structure) that lets Left/Right adjust a row offset and Up/Down cycle a 3-way glyph-source mode, then on any change closes and reopens a window and redraws a 4x8 grid of 32 glyph icons through Func_08019fcc/Func_0801a404/Func_08004080 depending on mode, and exits on the A/B mask read from the same ADDR_03001C94-style bits. Every callee's signature (Func_08019fcc, Func_0801a404, Func_0801eadc) is independently confirmed by three already-adopted exact owners, so the call shape here is solid; the remaining gap is entirely instruction scheduling/selection inside an otherwise-confirmed structure.

The raw m2c draft scored 520 vs 552 bytes, 123 wrong instructions, but its instruction-level diff showed the candidate's compiled loop physically duplicating: the four button-adjust checks were missing from the loop's first pass and only appeared after the 'continue', i.e. loop rotation the reference does not exhibit. Rewriting the m2c for(;;)/continue loop back into the literal labelled-goto form the raw disassembly actually uses (matching m2c's own loop_1: label) removed that duplication outright. Marking the ADDR_03001B04 hardware-register reads `volatile` (matching the family template's own `*(volatile u32 *)ADDR_03001B04` convention, which the raw m2c draft had silently dropped) stopped the compiler from caching one load across the four independent button checks the way a plain non-volatile read would, since the reference reloads the register fresh for each of the four checks. Together these took the draft to 524 vs 552 bytes, 121 wrong instructions -- and confirmed a first, more basic fix: the 'rows' redraw counter's modulo-8 is genuinely the `%` operator on a compile-time-constant power of two (the reference's negative-bias-then-shift sequence is gcc's standard signed-modulo-by-power-of-two expansion), not a call to the general Func_080022fc helper that the mode counter's modulo-3 genuinely does use.

Remaining disagreement is concentrated in register assignment for the same values (r1/r2/r3 swapped in the four button checks and in several Func_0801ea08 call sequences) and one place where the reference reloads a repeated literal '8' fifth argument fresh for three separate Func_0801ea08 calls while every candidate tried caches it in one register across all three -- the same unwanted-constant-reuse pattern seen on 08028c04, not resolved here either.
This reads as a genuine last-mile compiler-scheduling residual on an otherwise-confirmed structure, not a remaining source-shape or call-signature gap.
No external source, copied instruction bytes, inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, or compiler modification was used.
